correctness.rationale: The exact 4-existential closure test requires every pattern on every 4-vertex set to occur outside that set. Five-round Ehrenfeucht-Fraisse back-and-forth gives the exact equivalence with quantifier-rank <=5 theory of the countable Rado graph, and the rank-five four-extension axiom gives the converse. Translation and square scaling of finite fields reduce quadruples to two normalized initial pairs and (q−2)(q−3) unordered normal forms; the source code constructs genuine finite field quotients for q=9,25,49,81 and tests all eligible prime powers through 89. I independently evaluated all C(89,4)=2,441,626 four-vertex subsets directly via integer quadratic-residue adjacency and all 16 patterns: every subset passes. The supplied lower-order witness table and verified irreducible polynomials cover the thirteen smaller eligible q, so minimality is within the prime-power Paley family only.
